_comment: GPUs this project has actually run on, keyed by the name nvidia-smi
reports. Populated by scripts/gpu-registry.py, which every serving job
calls -- so a card nobody has seen before is recorded the first time a
job lands on it, rather than being guessed at later.
vram_mib and compute_cap are OBSERVED on the device. bandwidth_gbs is the
vendor figure and is the one number here that is not measured; it is what
the roofline prediction divides into the weight size. measured_tps holds
real single-stream decode rates per quantisation, which is what turns the
prediction into a calibration: this project has hit 79.7% and 80.0% of the
roofline on two very different cards, so bandwidth / weight_bytes * 0.8
predicts an untouched machine to within about 10%.

_notes: Turing TU102. No bf16, no FP8, no NVFP4, no Marlin -- which is what
rules out the W4A16 vLLM recipes the 4090 node uses.
Observed on the card: vram_mib 11264, compute_cap 7.5, 10820 MiB free
per card once headless. bandwidth_gbs is the vendor figure and is the
one number here that is not measured.
Two of these are PHB-connected on one NUMA node with NO NVLink bridge
fitted (nvidia-smi nvlink -s: all links inActive), so cross-card
traffic crosses PCIe and --split-mode row is not worth measuring.
